audit: No credible novel gene-diagnosis association survived scrutiny; every claim above is an established driver. The four strongest apparently novel signals (NOTCH2 in embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma 19/75, MED12 in ependymoma 15/81, NF2 in pilocytic astrocytoma 13/168, and the BCOR excess in medulloblastoma 26/212) are almost certainly fabricated or corrupted records: they carry protein positions far beyond the length of the protein (e.g. NOTCH2 p.E127469G, BCOR p.P101537F, NF2 p.P21404E) and/or missense/nonsense changes that no single-nucleotide substitution can produce (e.g. MED12 p.A1285Y, p.E1285C at the same residue with different reference amino acids), whereas the other ~62,000 codable mutations in the file contain zero such errors. I excluded those rows and do not report them; the data provenance should be investigated before any use. Other concerns: (1) ~18 hypermutated cases (>200 mutations, up to 15,731) were excluded because they would dominate gene-level counts; (2) highly recurrent identical calls in non-driver genes (C17orf80 p.S281R in 72 cases, HLTF p.Q898E, ZNF510 p.Q248E, CD69 p.L176Q, CD46, SLAMF7) look like germline or pipeline artifacts, though they were not diagnosis-specific; (3) diagnosis labels are heterogeneous and overlapping (Glioma malignant vs Astrocytoma vs Glioblastoma; RMS NOS vs embryonal; 'missing', 'Unknown', 'Neoplasm, NOS' groups) and many diagnoses have <10 cases; (4) BRAF V600E appears as p.V640E (alternate transcript) and fusions/CNVs (KIAA1549-BRAF, PAX-FOXO1, MYCN, C19MC) are invisible to an SNV/indel table, so frequencies for some entities are underestimates; (5) small-count hits (2 mutations in a tiny diagnosis group, e.g. RRAS2 in germinoma, CYP4F8 in large cell MB) reach nominal significance only because of sparse backgrounds and were not reported. I would not headline any new associations from this cohort.
methods: Per case, a gene was scored mutated if it had any non-synonymous somatic row. Cases with >200 mutations (hypermutators) were removed (1713 cases retained). Each mutation was checked for internal plausibility (protein position vs the gene's observed range; whether the ref->alt amino-acid change is reachable by one nucleotide substitution in the standard code); four gene-diagnosis clusters consisting of implausible records were removed. For each diagnosis vs all other cases I ran a one-sided Fisher exact test for every gene with >=2 mutated cases in that diagnosis, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction; claims were chosen from q<0.01 hits supported by known biology, with probability reflecting both statistical strength and prior knowledge, and expected frequency a shrunk version of the observed rate.
